statement.p: Find the maximum and minimum values of the function f(x)=x-\frac{8x}{x+2} on the interval [0,3].

static.solution: f(x) is the solution to f'(x)=0. The derivative isf'(x)=1-\frac{16}{\left(x+2\right)^{2}}. Setting this equal to zero and solving for x gives x=-2\pm 4, and of these two critical points only -2+4=2 lies in our interval. Evaluating f(-2+4)=f(2) yields the critical value -2. The values of the function at the endpoints of the interval are f(0)=0, f(3)=-1.8, so the minimum value is -2, and the maximum value is 0.
